CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found incidentally on chest imaging.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presented with a cough of approximately three months duration, initially off and on, which started after loading hay with horses. Patient loads approximately 400 bales per day. Subsequently developed a cold which prompted visit to primary care physician. PCP diagnosed bronchitis and ordered chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia, which revealed a lung nodule. CT scan was performed and confirmed the nodule. Patient was referred to thoracic surgery for further evaluation. Patient reports regular exercise including biking and typically does not get sick. Cough has since resolved. Denies current pain or shortness of breath.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain. Denies shortness of breath.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis, currently fair control, no recent flares. Previous smoker, quit approximately seven years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No family history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Active lifestyle with regular exercise and biking. Previous smoker, quit seven years ago. Works with horses, loads hay regularly. Prefers trail riding to road riding.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 124/76, heart rate 70, respiratory rate 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Afebrile. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no clicks, rubs, or murmurs, no extra beats. Extremities: skin pink, warm, and dry. No edema to lower extremities. Swelling noted on knuckles of third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe with smooth appearance. No emphysematous disease present.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper lobe lung nodule, incidentally found. Plan includes: pulmonary function tests to establish baseline lung function, PET CT to determine metabolic activity of nodule, and video-assisted thoracoscopy with removal of nodule and small portion of lung under general anesthesia (approximately 1.5 hours duration). Patient will be admitted post-procedure with chest tube, anticipated removal at bedside the following day, with expected one-night hospital stay. Rheumatoid arthritis: continue follow-up with rheumatologist and continue current medication therapy as previously outlined.
